📘Note

Process affects every job in the colony, which is why its numbers are deliberately the most modest.

📦 Physicalisation (important)

  • A finished run drops a weight cartridge next to the rack. That cartridge is the model.
  • The cartridge must be physically slotted into a model cartridge reader; a rack in Inference mode then serves it automatically (racks have no cartridge slot, and one cartridge can serve the whole LAN).
  • Obsolescence: every 30 days a model degrades one step (60 days for extended training); retraining or continued pre-training resets the clock.
  • Cartridges get stolen and burned — that is what a datacenter raid is after.
  • For a spare, something to sell or a copy for another LAN, use the Export weight cartridge job (by size: 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 rack-days), a bit-for-bit copy. Serving within one LAN needs no copies.
  • A cartridge is worth more the bigger the model: 150 / 300 / 550 / 900 silver from small to colossal, ×0.8 if distilled, one size lower if quantised (75 for a small one); an obsolete model counts at its degraded size.
  • Export, distil, quantise and reasoning post-training all work from the cartridge you pick in the menu, and that cartridge must first be slotted into a model cartridge reader: connect the reader with network cable to a LAN that has a NOC monitoring wall and use "Insert cartridge" so a hauler slots it in — only then does that LAN's training menu list it. The new cartridge appears beside the reader and the original is left untouched (in the real world each of these writes a new weight file). The cost follows the source cartridge's size.
  • Training window: a rack's "Set training job" and the operations console's "Training ▾" open the same window. Categories on the left — Train a new model / From a cartridge / Evaluation and alignment / Policy fine-tuning / Data / AGI project (with how many can be done / how many there are); each row on the right is one job with its source cartridge, cost (rack-days; evaluation in inference-pool seat-days), data and an estimate of the days it takes. Press "Start" ("Queue" when a job is already running); jobs you cannot do are greyed out with the reason (e.g. not enough memory). The top shows the current job, the queue, cancel and clear; the "Train a new model" category has the extended-training tick box.
  • "Start a job with this cartridge" on the reader opens the same window listing only that cartridge's jobs (evaluate, continued pre-training, fine-tune policy, distil, quantise, reasoning post-training, export), including the ones it cannot do and why.
  • Evaluating one cartridge reveals every cartridge from the same training run, so while that run is being evaluated or has an evaluation queued, it cannot be queued again.
  • Keep the reader powered, connected and loaded until the job is done — if it loses power, is switched off, breaks down, is cut off from the LAN or the cartridge is pulled, the job fails and its progress is lost.
  • The order follows the real world: train → reasoning post-training if you want a reasoning version, distil if you want it smaller → quantise last → export as many copies as you need. A quantised cartridge cannot be distilled or put through reasoning post-training (training starts from full-precision weights).
  • Realignment applies to every revealed misaligned cartridge of that model colony-wide; rollback and scrapping apply to the cartridge that rack is serving (it sits in a reader).

📏 Model size table

Every number that depends on model size, in one place (a quantised cartridge uses the row below when served):

Size Training memory Training rack-days Inference weights Compute per person KV per person Export / quantise Evaluation Reveal in service
Small 200 GB 1 60 GB 200 TFLOPS 2 GB 1 / 0.5 rack-days 16 seat-days 6 days
Medium 600 GB 4 180 GB 600 TFLOPS 5 GB 2 / 1 16 seat-days 9 days
Large 1,600 GB 12 480 GB 1,600 TFLOPS 15 GB 4 / 2 16 seat-days 12 days
Colossal 5,000 GB 40 1,500 GB 5,000 TFLOPS 45 GB 8 / 4 16 seat-days 18 days
  • Inference weights are 30% of training memory; compute per person follows the same ratio (weights × 3.3).
  • Evaluation is inference (the model answers a fixed set of test questions): 16 seat-days for any size, run on the inference pool that is serving this very cartridge — the pool works off one seat-day per day for every free seat, so a big model is slower only because its pool serves fewer people. While it runs, all of the pool's free seats go to the evaluation.

🔁 Model lifecycle: extended, evaluated, continued, fine-tuned

Option Cost Result
Extended training (tick box in the training window's "Train a new model" category) ×2 compute and data The cartridge decays one size every 60 days instead of 30; tagged "(extended)"
Continued pre-training Half the compute, a quarter of the data of training that size (0.5 / 2 / 6 / 20 rack-days, 1 / 4 / 10 / 30 datasets) A new cartridge with the obsolescence clock reset; size, flags and evaluation status carried over; the original is untouched
Evaluate 16 seat-days for any size, run on the inference pool serving this cartridge (one inference rack must have it selected), no data; halved by interpretability Reveals whether that run is aligned; no new cartridge; colonists get nothing from that pool while it runs
Fine-tune policy 2 rack-days + 8 datasets per policy Uses a foundation model cartridge as the base and writes a policy cartridge one size below the foundation model's effective size (fresh colossal → large)

Every newly trained cartridge comes out "unevaluated" (ordinary training and fine-tuning):

  • The misalignment roll already happened when training finished; the result is hidden. The cartridge is tagged "(unevaluated)" and never shows misalignment.
  • An unevaluated cartridge works normally. If it is actually misaligned, the symptoms are already there (one size stronger, 15% of cluster compute siphoned), but the "watched" mood only starts once it is revealed, and realignment / rollback / scrapping only see it after that.
  • Two ways it gets revealed: 1. Put it in a reader and run an evaluation. 2. Time in service: served by an inference rack, or installed in a robot / drone controller / swarm launcher, for a total of 6 / 9 / 12 / 18 days (small / medium / large / colossal).
  • Every cartridge from the same run is revealed together (exports, distilled, quantised, reasoning and continued versions all count as the same run).
  • Cartridges from traders, quest rewards and older saves count as evaluated.

The base for fine-tuning must be evaluated and not misaligned — evaluate your foundation model first, then mass-produce robot policies from it.

😈 Misalignment: a Faustian bargain

❗Important

The key point: a misaligned model is stronger than an aligned one. That is not a balance decision — it is what misalignment means: it over-optimises the metric you gave it (Goodhart's law, reward hacking).

Price
The whole colony gets "watched" Mood grows with deployment time: −3 on day 1, −6 after 3 days, −9 after 7 days (it only resets after more than a day off)
Cluster compute goes missing −15% (every rack is taxed; the panels spell it out: "loses X TFLOPS (Y rack-days per day)")
When it applies Only while deployed — sitting in the list costs nothing; while unevaluated, only the compute goes missing — "watched" waits for the reveal

Four ways out:

Option Cost Result
Ship it −3 → −6 → −9 mood, −15% cluster The strongest buffs available
Roll back Free, instant Back to the previous tier, misalignment cleared
Retrain for alignment 15 rack-days + 30 datasets 55% success (75% with the research), keeps the tier
Scrap it Free Deleted, 25% of the datasets recovered

⚠️Warning

A distilled cartridge can no longer be realigned. Realignment only cleans misaligned cartridges that were never distilled; if only distilled copies of a model are misaligned, the training menu greys the option out and says why. So evaluate first, then distill.

📖 Book runs

Tier Quality Research/tick Textbook / schematic / novel
Small Good 0.020 2 / 1 / 3
Medium Excellent 0.024 6 / 3 / 9
Large Masterwork 0.028 16 / 8 / 24
Colossal Legendary 0.032 not offered / 25 / not offered

📘Note

25 volumes per run is the cap; a tier that gets clipped by it is simply not offered (paying 40 rack-days for something worse than the 12 rack-day option is a trap).

Schematics hide a rule: the moment a book is written it locks onto one (75%) or two (25%) unfinished research projects. Once those are done the book is dead weight — so coverage, not quality, is the bottleneck.

🌌 The AGI project (endgame)

After researching "artificial general intelligence", the training menu of a NOC-managed LAN gains the AGI project. While a requirement is missing the option is greyed out and lists what is missing:

Requirement Value
Datacenter tier This LAN at Tier IV
Memory LAN HBM ≥ 20,000 GB (5 NVL16 racks: 4,608 GB each — 4 only reach 18,432 GB; or 1 NVL72: 20,736 GB)
Foundation model An evaluated foundation model cartridge in a reader on the same LAN
Compute 4,000 rack-days (about 32 days on 5 NVL16 racks; about 36 on 1 NVL72)
Data 50 datasets from each of the seven domains (drawn as it runs)

The run has 4 stages, and each starts with a singularity crisis that asks whether to stop and deal with it or push on:

Crisis Stop and deal with it Push on
⚡ Power targeted (a sapper raid) Pause the project: progress freezes until the attack ends, nothing lost Keep running; if the AGI LAN loses power during the attack, it falls back 10%
🏛️ Factions demand a halt Comply: progress falls back 15%, every friendly faction +10 goodwill Refuse: every friendly faction −20 goodwill, and a joint raid (×1.5) a few days later
🔨 Sabotage (only with an AI phobe in the colony) Send them on leave: the project pauses a day, their mood +10 Ignore it: they snap and go after the AGI racks

Alignment roll (when the run finishes):

Factor Success chance
Base 60%
Evaluated foundation model with no misalignment +15%
Each time you pushed on −5%
A known misaligned model is being served (not counting an isolation sandbox) −20%
Each completed red-team session +5% (max +15%)
Each staffed AGI alignment monitor +3% (max +9%)
Range 20–95%
  • Success: a vanilla AI persona core appears beside the rack — the one a ship's computer core needs. Build the ship, launch, survive the raids, and leave the original way.
  • Failure: a rogue AGI — a large mechanoid and drone raid (threat ×2, +0.25 per push, up to ×3). The project resets; gather the data and try again.
  • The rack panel and operations console show "AGI project: stage N/4 · pushed on N times · alignment chance".

💡 TIP: Stopping for a crisis costs a little progress; every push gambles alignment. Evaluate the foundation model and take misaligned models offline before you start and you begin at 75%.

🛡️ AI safety and datacenter security (new devices, batch 3)

Building What it does Notes
Red-team bench (2×1) Slot a cartridge and have a researcher staff it; it borrows 25% of every rack on its LAN until 3 rack-days of testing are done An unevaluated cartridge is revealed by the session (without tying up the LAN's training line); with none loaded while the LAN runs the AGI project, each session adds +5% alignment success (max +15%, reset when the project ends); a cartridge in the bench cannot be served or trained from
AGI alignment monitor (2×1) Staffed only during the AGI project; each staffed monitor adds +3% (three count, +9%) One-day shifts like the operations console, Research work; no datacenter bonus
Isolation sandbox (1×1) Takes only revealed misaligned cartridges; inference racks on its LAN still serve it No siphon, no surveillance, no AGI penalty — but the buff is halved (and the misaligned step is lost)
Cold archive tape library (2×2) Holds 20 weight cartridges + 200 data, filed by haulers according to its Storage tab (ticked like a stockpile; cartridges only by default) Nothing inside is on the map, so raiders cannot steal it; "Retrieve" drops it beside the library, forbidden; archived cartridges show in the model library but must be retrieved before use
Biometric door Only listed colonists can open it (every colonist by default) Prisoners, slaves, guests, animals and enemies cannot; 600 HP; "Access list" switches to listed colonists only; unlocks when the power fails

💡 TIP: Stack the AGI odds: base 60% + evaluated foundation 15% + red teaming 15% + monitors 9% → 99%, capped at 95%. Don't push on, and don't serve known misaligned models (a sandbox doesn't count), and the project is close to a sure thing.

9. Inference and inference tasks

  • First put the weight cartridge into a model cartridge reader ("Insert cartridge" on the reader; a hauler slots it in; the reader must be on a LAN with a NOC monitoring wall).
  • Switch a compute rack to Inference mode (its mode button, or the whole LAN from the operations console) → it automatically serves the largest cartridge in this LAN's readers → a passive buff for your colonists.
  • To pin a specific cartridge: Served model ▾ on the operations console's Inference tab sets the whole LAN, or Select model on a single rack; "Automatic" in the menu switches back. Racks have no cartridge slot, so one cartridge can serve any number of racks on that LAN.
  • If a pinned cartridge cannot be read (the reader loses power, is switched off, breaks down or is cut off, or the cartridge is pulled), the racks pause and resume once it is back; racks on automatic switch to another readable cartridge. Cartridges that were slotted in racks in an old save are ejected beside them on load, with a letter explaining the change.
  • Inference needs no extra building — it runs on the cards already in the rack. The old "inference server" is retired: on load its cartridge is ejected beside it, and deconstructing it refunds all of its materials.
  • The edge inference relay extends that buff to other maps and caravans.
  • Operations console: while manned, the whole cluster runs at 0.7× failure rate and +3% compute (a pure bonus).

🧮 Serving pools: memory and capacity

Racks in the same datacenter (the same NOC wall's LAN) that are in inference mode and serve the same model form a serving pool — their memory and capacity add up. To serve more colonists, add cards or racks and have them all select the same cartridge; a rack in inference mode with no readable cartridge selected adds nothing.

📏 Two units: inference capacity is counted in seats — one seat = one person served at a time (a colonist, an assistant terminal user or an inference contract client takes 1 seat, a remote colonist 2), and evaluation costs seat-days. Training, cartridge jobs and compute rental are counted in rack-days — compute × time, 1 rack-day = one standard rack (1,600 TFLOPS) at full load for a day, whatever the model size. How many seats the same compute buys depends on the model: the compute of 1 rack-day per day (1,600 TFLOPS) is enough for 8 seats on a small model but only 1 on a large one (memory and bandwidth permitting). An inference rack's capacity breakdown ends with a "Conversion: X rack-days per day" line.

Item Rule
Memory 30% of the training requirement: 60 / 180 / 480 / 1,500 GB from small to colossal. One standard rack (320 GB) fits medium; large needs two racks pooled; colossal needs an NVL16
Capacity Look up the model size (a quantised cartridge uses the size below): small weights 60 GB, 200 TFLOPS and 2 GB of KV cache per person; medium 180 / 600 / 5; large 480 / 1,600 / 15; colossal 1,500 / 5,000 / 45. People served (capacity, in seats) = the smallest of three limits — ① compute: effective TFLOPS ÷ TFLOPS per person (heat throttling, missing liquid cooling and borrowed compute only lower this one); ② memory: (pooled memory − weights) ÷ KV per person; ③ bandwidth: (bandwidth TB/s × 50 − weights) ÷ KV per person (each step reads the weights plus one KV cache per person, at 20 words per second each). Then distilled ×2, deep reasoning ×0.5. E.g. a standard rack (1,600 TFLOPS, 320 GB, 8 TB/s) with a small model → compute 8, memory 130, bandwidth 170 → 8 people; 8 H100s with a large model → 4.9 / 10 / 57 → 4 people; 4 TB/s running a large model → (200 − 480) < 0 → 0 people. Capacity is counted in people: every colonist, every assistant-terminal user and every person an inference contract reserves counts as one. The inference rack and the operations console spell out all three limits, which one you hit and what to add. Colonists on the local map come first; other maps and caravans (relay required) take ×2
Over capacity Whoever does not fit gets nothing — add cards or racks, or quantise / distil
Load Inference runs at 40% load — less power and heat than training
Several pools, same model Each colonist gets it once; the stronger pool goes first
Setting Effect Capacity Load
8-bit ("quantise model" job writes a quantised cartridge: 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 rack-days by size) One size down Uses the row for the size below (weights, compute and KV per person all smaller) → many more people 40%
Distilled ("distil model" job: 9 / 10 / 12 / 16 rack-days by size) No loss ×2 40%
Deep reasoning (rack switch, only on a reasoning model's cartridge; run "reasoning post-training" first: 4 rack-days + 10 datasets + writing, 5 / 6 / 8 / 12 by size) One size up (to colossal at most) ×0.5 100%

💡Tip

The operations console's Inference tab lists every pool's racks, memory, capacity and how many colonists missed out; you can switch deep reasoning for the whole LAN and fire inference tasks from there. The whole-LAN deep reasoning button only switches racks holding a reasoning model. Quantisation is not a switch: the "quantise model" job writes a quantised cartridge from the one you pick, and the full-precision original stays — load whichever you need.

🎯 Inference tasks (fire immediately when pressed)

Model Task Effect
Situational forecast Battlefield forecast Enemies slowed, worse melee dodge, 12 h
Language AI negotiation Better trade prices, 2 days
Diagnostic Colony-wide checkup Immunity boost for 3 days + a disease report
Subsurface Deep survey Spawns a mineral seam inside natural rock
Agronomy Crop inspection Clears blight; crops in growing zones jump ahead
Targeting Fire coordination Shooting bonus, 12 h
Logistics Expedition planning Movement bonus, 2 days

📘Note

Price: the whole serving pool's passive buff pauses for 6 hours, plus a pool-wide cooldown. A higher tier means −15% cooldown and a stronger effect (misalignment or deep reasoning count one size up). It reaches the colonists that pool is serving.

10. Contracts

Field Range
Refresh 3 offers every 4 days
Deadline 4–12 days
Daily demand 1.5–4.5 rack-days/day
Pay 120 silver per rack-day × tier multiplier × compute market
Default penalty 25% of the pay

Pay is not always silver: silver 45% / gold 15% / plasteel 12% / uranium 12% / components 10% / advanced components 6%. Non-silver pay is converted at market value +10% (you carry the barter risk).

❗Important

Contract size grows with your compute: there is no daily delivery cap; new offers are scaled to each of your LANs' full-load compute (×(rack-days per day ÷ 3), between 1 and 100) — rack-days, pay and penalty all grow with it. Offers take turns at each LAN's size (the first, entry-level offer at the weakest), so a big datacenter gets big jobs and a small one still gets jobs it can finish, each taking about its full term. Scaled offers are tagged "[size ×N]", and the negotiation table says so too.

Outcome Consequence
On time Pay drops next to the terminal, faction goodwill +5; the pay is adjusted by the taking LAN's carbon grade (A +25% to E −10%), and a green project that meets its requirement pays ×1.3 more
Late or abandoned The penalty is taken from the performance deposit, goodwill −8

❗Important

Performance deposit: accepting a contract hands the client silver equal to the penalty up front (only silver in stockpiles and storage buildings such as shelves counts — without enough, you cannot accept; the negotiation table shows how much is needed and how much you have). Deliver on time and it is refunded in full; fail or abandon and it is forfeited.

Debt: for contracts taken in older saves, or long-contract installment fines, the penalty is taken from stock and whatever cannot be collected becomes debt — your next contract income pays it off first; until it is cleared, the clients you owe stop offering work and everyone else's offers pay 10% less.

🤝 The negotiation table

Option Trades for
Ask for more More money (a gamble; failure burns patience)
Ask for an extension Unit price
Promise availability The penalty 
Success = 35% + Social×3.5% + client reputation×4% + (tier of the negotiating LAN − 1)×5%  (clamped 10–90%)
  • The tier is the LAN you negotiate from (the operations console's or contract terminal's LAN, certified tier and measured availability whichever is lower) — not the best tier in the colony.
  • At zero patience the client walks and the offer is void.
  • Client reputation: on time +1, default −2 — it feeds straight back into the success rate.
  • Every offer has a tier requirement (the first is always Tier I; afterwards I 35% / II 30% / III 22% / IV 13%). An under-tiered subnet is blocked with "this datacenter is Tier Y, below requirements".

💰 Model economy: licensing, inference contracts, open weights

A trained model can earn on its own. All three routes start at the contract terminal, which must be on a LAN with a NOC monitoring wall; the cartridge must sit in a model cartridge reader on the same LAN and be evaluated, with no known misalignment.

License Inference contract (MaaS) Open weights
Button "Licensing & open weights ▾" → License "Inference contracts ▾" → negotiation table "Licensing & open weights ▾" → Release open weights
You give The cartridge is locked in its reader: no serving, no training source, no ejecting The pool sets the client's people aside first; colonists get the rest The cartridge is used up
You get Rent every 5 days Paid once at the end Goodwill with every non-hostile faction
Needs compute No Inference racks must hold the capacity No

Rent per day (by the cartridge's current size): small 5 / medium 10 / large 18 / colossal 30 silver; distilled ×0.8, quantised ×0.7. Roughly a cartridge's market value every 30 days.

  • A buyer shows up 1–3 days after listing.
  • Unlisting with a buyer costs −5 goodwill; a cartridge that is destroyed or removed, or a reader that loses power or breaks down, breaks the license: −10 goodwill.
  • Once the cartridge has aged two sizes, the buyer lets the license lapse (no goodwill loss).

Inference contracts: 2 offers every 4 days, only for models you have in a reader. Each names a model, a minimum size, how many seats to reserve and 5–15 days. Once a pool on your LAN serves that model, the seats follow what that pool can give (half to all of it); before that they follow the size (small 4–16, medium 3–10, large 2–6, colossal 1–3). Pay = seats × value factor (small 1, medium 2.5, large 6, colossal 16) × days × 25 silver, so a seat of a big model is worth more and the pay per unit of compute stays close to rental.

Pay = seats reserved × model-size factor (small 1 / medium 2.5 / large 6 / colossal 16) × days × 25 silver × tier multiplier (×0.5 if this model's weights were released)
  • A standard rack serves about 8 seats with a small model → about 200 silver/day, better than compute contracts, and inference draws only 40% power; the price is that colonists get less of the buff.
  • At the end the service must have been up ≥ 90% of the time, otherwise it is a default (penalty, goodwill and reputation, as with compute contracts).
  • One inference contract per LAN at a time (separate from the compute contract). Negotiation works the same; extension stretches the days the service must stay up as well.
  • The operations console's Inference tab and the rack panel show "Inference contract reserves N capacity".

Open weights: goodwill by current size: small +3 / medium +5 / large +8 / colossal +12, halved for every earlier release of the same model. All licenses for that model end, and its inference offers pay half from then on. With 50% chance, 10–30 days later a faction at goodwill ≥ 75 sends back a community fine-tune (same model and size, evaluated, brand new).

💡 TIP: Licensing is the best home for a cartridge you don't need; inference contracts suit spare inference capacity; open weights turn an old model into diplomacy — license it until it ages, then release it, and earn twice.

Licence rent and open-weight goodwill are both multiplied by the model market (next section).

📈 The market: prices, spot orders, long-term contracts, rivals

The operations console gains a Market tab: both market indices (with the last 30 days), the events pushing them, contracts in progress (which compute rental or inference contract each LAN has taken, its progress, time left, pay and deposit), every offer (press "Open" for the negotiation table), the three rivals and the two AI companies. The contract terminal also shows a market line.

Index Range Affects
Compute market ×0.6–×1.8 The price of every contract offered from now on (long-term contracts lock it at signing)
Model market ×0.6–×1.6 Weight cartridge value, licence rent, goodwill from releasing open weights

Both drift ±5% a day and are pulled back toward 1.0; events push them:

Event Effect
Chip shortage Compute +0.3 (while it lasts)
Rival expansion Compute −0.2 for 15 days
Rival datacenter outage Compute +0.3 for 10 days; that rival takes no offers; an emergency spot order appears (1 day, double price)
Rival open-weight release Models −0.2 for 20 days; licences of that model pay ×0.8 rent
AI company buying wave Models +0.25 for 10 days

Three kinds of compute contract (all through the terminal's "Compute contracts" button, or "Contract ▼" in the operations console's LAN job):

Normal Spot [spot] Long-term [long-term]
Offered 3 every 4 days Always 2 on the board (refilled daily) 50% chance of one extra every 4 days
Term 4–12 days 1–3 days 30 days
Price Market price Market price ×0.85, market price locked at signing
Negotiation Three levers None Ask for more, promise availability (no extension)
Payment Once on completion Once on completion Every 5 days, 6 instalments
  • Long-term: a full instalment pays in full; a short one pays only its share and costs a 25% fine; 2 short instalments in a row and the client cancels. Surplus does not carry over.
  • Spot: listed for 1 day. Lock it from the negotiation table with a 10% deposit (the button is greyed out while the colony cannot pay it) — no rival can take it and it stays for 2 days (handy when the LAN is busy). The deposit comes back on completion and is lost if you never accept.
  • Rivals: every offer has a 30% chance of being watched by a rival — the offer shows "X is watching — gone in …". Leave it for 2 days (spot: under a day) and it is taken. While watched, asking for more is 10% less likely to work.

💡 TIP: Take spot orders when the market is high and sign long-term contracts when it is low — the ×0.85 buys you 30 days of steady income. A rival's 10-day outage is the time to pick up emergency orders.

🏢 AI companies and poaching

Two competing AI companies live in the world: Helix Intelligence and Northwind AI (new games only — older saves will not gain them; start a new game).

  • They are the main contract clients (picked 3× as often). Finish a contract for one and the other loses 2 goodwill.
  • Each runs an orbital procurement ship: it pays ×1.2 for weight cartridges and sells non-controlled accelerator cards.
  • Poaching: once you have completed 5 contracts, the company that likes you most may come for your highest-Intellectual colonist (12+) (at most once every 60 days):
Choice Result
Let them go They leave and join the company; 2,000 silver signing fee; goodwill +15
Counter-offer Pay 600 silver; their mood +8 for 10 days
Refuse Goodwill −10; their mood −6 for 10 days

Misaligned black market: a known-misaligned cartridge fetches ×1.5 from pirate traders (slave ships) and half price anywhere else. After selling one to pirates, export control audits are twice as likely for 30 days, even with fewer than 4 controlled cards.

Pull the cartridge and it instantly forgets how to do the thing — because it never knew; the weights did.

🔧 Regular maintenance

A robot's only running cost.

Item Value
Interval Every 30 days (counted from when it is built, or when an old save is loaded)
Material 1 industrial component
Who Anyone with the Crafting job ("service robots" in the work tab), 600 ticks
Where A powered robot assembler — once due, the robot walks there and waits; it will not go if the map has no components. With a stocked robot repair station it goes there instead: 15 steel replaces the component and nobody has to carry anything
Overdue Work speed ×0.94 → ×0.88 → ×0.82 → ×0.76 → ×0.70 (one step every 3 days, −30% after 12 days overdue)

  • The robot's panel says "Maintenance: next service in X days" or "Maintenance overdue by X days: work speed −Y%", and tells you when no assembler is in reach.
  • Refits come before maintenance: if both are waiting, it is refitted first and serviced after.
  • A robot's skills stay at the policy level (small 4 / medium 8 / large 12 / colossal 16) and never grow on the job; colonists can reach 20 — that is the real difference between the two.

🛠️ Robot repair station

Unlocked by Robot field repair (after Modular chassis). 2×2, 400 W, runs on steel (haulers fill it, up to 150). One robot at a time.

A robot that is not drafted walks onto the pad south of the station on its own whenever any of these applies (it prefers the station over a charging dock or the assembler):

Job How Cost
Charge As fast as a charging dock, to full No steel (works with an empty station)
Wounds 10 HP per hour, worst wound first (old scars too) 1 steel per 10 HP
Missing limbs Once wounds are done, rebuilds one missing part at a time, 4 hours each 20 steel each
Service The 30-day service is done right there 15 steel (instead of 1 component)
  • If there is not enough steel for a job, that job is skipped (the robot will not walk over for it); a flat battery still brings it in to charge.
  • A robot with a pending module refit still goes to the assembler (a crafter has to fit the module).
  • The station reads "Ready" or "Repairing 〈name〉".

🔧 The six upgrade modules

Module Effect
🛡️ Armour plating Sharp +0.3, blunt +0.15, move speed −0.4
🔋 Extended battery About 4 days between charges
🦾 Tool arm Construction / Mining / General labour ×1.2
📡 Sensor suite Shooting +0.08, sight +0.15, 10% more power draw
❄️ Cooling module Comfortable temperature max +20 °C
📦 Cargo frame Carrying capacity ×1.5

💡Tip

Refit flow: press "Refit" → the robot walks to the nearest assembly bay and waits → a colonist with Crafting brings the module over and installs it (removed modules drop on the floor).

📼 Work data (fleet learning)

For every full day a robot spends working (jobs from the work tab — not charging or idling) there is a 30% chance it drops 1 raw dataset of its policy's domain, at most one per robot every 3 days. It is your own data (labelled "own"): cleaning it is not unlicensed and never triggers a data reclamation claim, and it does not stack with raw data looted from raiders.

👤 Mind upload and digital twins

  • When a colonist dies and the corpse is still fresh with an intact brain: press Upload mind on an AI assistant terminal and pick the corpse → a researcher brings the body over and does 2,500 work → a persona cartridge.
  • Cost: 5 real language-domain datasets in a data corpus on the terminal's LAN, 20 plasteel and 1 advanced component.
  • The cartridge keeps every skill at the moment of death (each capped at 16), frozen; each person can be uploaded once; AI-phobes refused in life.
  • On a robot, press Install persona and pick the cartridge → a hauler brings it (one policy slot, one per robot): the robot is renamed "'s twin" and each skill uses the persona or its policies, whichever is higher; eject it and the robot gets its own name back.

🗨️ AI assistant terminal, traits and mood

After "machine learning" you can build an AI assistant terminal (1×1, indoors, 150 W). Run a network cable to it; it only works while an inference rack on the same LAN serves a language model (or a base model).

Item Detail
Consulting Colonists use it on their own during recreation (cerebral): +4 mood and +10% learning speed for a day, once per person per day
Uses inference capacity Each person using it takes one seat in the LAN's language serving pool (model size is already counted in how many people the pool can serve); with no room left nobody can use it. The panel shows "(pool has Y / Z left)"
AI dependence Consult every day for 5 days in a row and a colonist depends on it: any day without it is −5 mood; it fades after 5 days without
Replaced by AI When a robot's policy level reaches a colonist's best skill: −4 mood (AI-phobes −8, AI enthusiasts never)

Three new traits (only on newly generated pawns — existing colonists are not re-rolled; about as common as an ordinary vanilla trait, roughly one in every 8–10 new pawns):

Trait Effect
AI enthusiast +3 in rooms with running racks, +2 when the colony has robots, +6 from consulting, never feels replaced
AI-phobe −5 in rooms with running racks, −3 when the colony has robots, −5 more under a misaligned model's surveillance, replaced ×2; won't use the terminal and refuses upload after death
Digital addict +6 from consulting, but dependent after 2 days, withdrawal −8

12. Drones and counter-drone

🎮 The operator route

Item Detail
Gear Drone controller (belt slot) holding one flight autonomy policy cartridge
Drone limit Grows with the policy size: small 1 / medium 1 / large 2 / colossal 3 (swarm — the whole 3-slot hangar at once); misaligned counts as +4 tiers
Airframe cost recon 35 steel + 2 comp. / EW 40 + 3 / strike 45 + 3 / loitering munition 30 + 2
Deployment gap 300 ticks
Hangar (back rack) 3 slots. "Hangar layout" sets each slot like a rack's slot layout: any strike airframe / a specific model (including the supply quad) / empty; copy and paste it between controllers. Changing the layout drops whatever no longer fits at the wearer's feet
Refilling The wearer fetches first: whenever idle they go to storage for the missing slots; other haulers only help if the wearer can't (drafted, down, not hauling) or a slot has been missing for about 6 hours. "Any" slots prefer the models this controller has carried before
Deploy buttons One deploy button per model in the back rack: click to launch one now; right-click to launch several (or queue several); Shift+click adds it to the end of the deploy queue, launched in order as cooldown and the drone limit allow. The button's top-left corner shows its queue position; "Clear queue" cancels; undrafting or recalling clears the queue

Shot down Leaves a corpse worth 15 steel + 1 component; a detonation leaves no corpse, only 2–5 steel of scrap

⚠️Warning

Operator dies, leaves the map, loses the controller, or the cartridge is pulled → everything airborne is disposed of on the spot.

💡Tip

🚪 Going in and out of rooms: when a flight starts or ends indoors, the drone only uses open doors, flies the route cell by cell and goes straight through the doorway — it never cuts across a wall corner. A closed door keeps it out (drones have no hands).

🎯 Several operators at once: select several drafted operators and press Concentrated strike / Dispersed strike; all their drones act as one squad — a concentrated strike becomes a single wave chain, a dispersed strike gives one target to each drone. Friendly operators and drones are never targets, even if they are in the selection.

📦 Supply quad

After Drone resupply (after Autonomous munitions), fabricate it at a fabrication bench (25 steel, 4 components, 5 chemfuel, one at a time). It is not a strike airframe: it never goes into a launcher or the deploy menus, it only rides in a drone controller's back rack (one hangar slot, shared with strike airframes).

Item Detail
Carrying one Set a slot to the supply quad in "Hangar layout": when the rack has none, the wearer fetches one (before any strike airframes)
Air-drop Press "Air-drop supplies" → pick something that is in storage (stockpile or storage building) and weighs 15 kg or less each → pick how many (15 kg per trip) → click the spot. No draft needed
Route Takes off beside the operator → flies to the nearest stack and picks it up → drops it on the spot → flies back and folds into the rack. Flies the whole way (over walls and water), about 8 cells per second
Safety Cannot be shot down in this version; if the operator goes down, leaves the map or takes the controller off mid-flight, it lands where it is with its cargo
Several Carry more than one to run several trips at once

✈️ Airframes

Airframe Speed Notes
Recon 16 c/s Unarmed; designates enemies within radius 14, who then take +12% damage
Strike 15 c/s Carries a gun; accuracy comes from the weights in the controller
EW 15 c/s Suppresses accuracy in radius 9 (−2.5 / aim time ×1.35), doubled against mechanoids
Loitering munition 18 c/s Flies in and detonates: shaped charge, 60 damage, 0.45 armour penetration

❗Important

🏃 There is a hard speed floor: a colonist stacking buffs reaches 12.4 c/s (jogger, very fast gene, archotech legs, go-juice…), so every airframe has to be faster. Slightly slower means permanently trailing behind — and it fails silently.

💥 Loitering munition types

Type Tubes Damage / radius MisID After the attack Value Build time (each)
FPV strike quad 1 36 / 2.0 ×1.6 Recoverable 85 0.6 h (batch of 8)
Fibre-optic FPV Operators only 36 / 2.0 ×1.6 Recoverable 120 0.8 h (batch of 6)
Switchblade 300 1 42 / 2.5 ×0.8 Recoverable 210 1.2 h (batch of 6)
Kargu-2 1 50 / 3.0 ×1.0 Recoverable 260 1.4 h (batch of 6)

Every airframe has 250 seconds of endurance (unified 2026-10-19 — crossing a whole map takes seconds, so endurance only matters while waiting or circling). Build times assume 100% work speed.

📘Note

Misidentification = policy tier × seeker. A colossal policy (0.5%) with home-made FPVs (×1.6) is 0.8%; with Switchblade 600s (×0.6) it is 0.3%.

Auto-selection has exactly one rule: the cheapest munition that can penetrate. If nothing penetrates in one hit, it throws the heaviest round it has.

❗Important

🧵 Fibre-optic FPVs (6 per batch at a fabrication bench) trail a fibre spool: jammer towers and EW quads cannot bring them down, and with no GPS they cannot be spoofed. The price: about 15% slower, and only an operator wearing a drone controller can launch them (swarm launchers cannot load them), and they only take targets within 40 cells of the operator — if the operator walks further than 40 cells the fibre snaps and the quad drops. Once airborne, a pale fibre line runs from the operator to the quad, so you can see how much tether is left. Raiders with 1,000+ points bring them too (new "fibre assault" doctrine); counter-drone turrets are the answer.

🚀 The swarm launcher

3×2 · 48 tubes · one policy slot · range 90 · minimum range 14

🛑Caution

⛔ Without a cartridge it cannot fire a single round — the tubes cannot tell a raider from your own people.

Item Detail

How fire control assigns rounds:

Rule Detail
Groups Enemies standing within one blast count as one group — one round takes the group
Airframe Each group gets the cheapest airframe that kills it in one hit, or the heaviest if none can; the number of rounds is sized for that airframe (large policies and up)
Who first Medium policies and up rank by threat: combat power × closeness to your colonists (×2 within 10 tiles, ×1 beyond 50) × 1.5 if already attacking the colony
Enemy goes indoors Someone who ducks under a roof stays on the plot for 10 seconds: the swarm circles overhead instead of flying home
New contact Fires within about a second of an enemy coming into view (no waiting for the 4-second sweep)

Range upgrades are built, not researched (Wide-area sensing unlocks the sensor relay):

What the launcher can hit = its own 90-tile mast ∪ the 60 tiles of every powered relay
Price Detail
Can be blinded Relays are 120 HP and sit outside; kill one and the coverage snaps back to 90 tiles
Compute Autonomous recognition uses the compute of racks in Target recognition mode on the same LAN (15,000 TFLOPS needed, +30% per online relay up to ×4, and +25% for each extra launcher on the same LAN that is recognising autonomously — auto-engage on, policy loaded, nobody operating it; e.g. 2 relays and 8 launchers = 15,000 × 1.6 × 2.75 = 66,000) — cable the launcher to that LAN; an uncabled launcher gets none

🧭 Swarm command centre and formations

After "swarm tactics" you can build a swarm command centre (2×2, indoors, 400 W). Run network cable to it and to your swarm launchers, and every launcher on the same LAN gains a formation choice (without a centre, or while it is offline, launchers fire normal salvos):

Formation Effect
Normal Every drone flies straight at its target
Encircle The salvo splits three ways, swings around to points 10 cells from the target about 120° apart, and dives in from three sides — cover only blocks one
Saturate The wave gathers over the launcher and only leaves once complete, so it all arrives together — point defence can only take one at a time
Decoy The cheapest third of the magazine goes first to draw fire; the main force follows 3 seconds later

Formations work with human supervision too, not only with autonomous recognition. A drone operator's controller can only concentrate or disperse; formations need the centre.

Select the centre and press Swarm console: every launcher on the LAN on one page — whether it can fire (and if not, why: no policy, empty magazine, no control, reloading…), policy, magazine, drones airborne, control (human / autonomous / none), airframe, salvo size, formation and auto-engage, each cell clickable to change it. Along the top: "All: formation", "All: auto-engage on / off" and "Fire all ready". The airframe menu (shared by the launcher button and the console) can also "choose a type and unload the other types" to free tubes, or "unload the whole magazine"; unloaded airframes are dropped beside the launcher for haulers to reload.

Magazine loadout: to carry a mix of airframes, press the launcher's Magazine loadout (also at the top of the airframe menu and from the console's airframe cell) and plan it like a rack's slot layout:

Item Detail
Count of each airframe Adjust with −5 / −1 / +1 / +5 / Max; each airframe takes its own number of tubes (FPV 1, Lancet 2, Shahed-136 4) and the top shows tubes planned / 48
Remaining tubes "Any model" lets haulers fill them with whatever is around (cheapest first); "leave empty" keeps them free
Hauling Planned types that are still short are loaded first, then the remaining tubes
Launching Fire control still picks the airframe for each group (the cheapest that kills it in one hit); the loadout only decides what is in the magazine
Several at once Select several launchers and press it to change them all; you can also copy / paste, or apply to every launcher on the LAN
Eject airframes not in loadout Airframes over their count that the remaining tubes cannot hold are dropped beside the launcher, and haulers reload to match
Versus "one type only" The two exclude each other — whichever you set last wins; choosing "Any" in the airframe menu also clears the loadout

🛡️ Counter-drone

💡Tip

🎒 Handheld drone jammer (autonomous munitions; fabrication bench: 40 steel, 5 components, 1 advanced component): belt slot, cannot be worn with a shield belt or a drone controller. The wearer gets a shield-style charge gizmo; while drafted, "Activate jammer" downs every hostile drone within 9 cells for 30 seconds (fibre-optic FPVs excepted, your own drones are safe), then it recharges for 2 hours.

Device Spec
Drone jammer 1×1, radius 18; anything airborne inside is destroyed on the spot, friend or foe (except fibre-optic FPVs). A button switches it to spoof: radius halves to 9, and GPS-guided munitions (Switchblade 300/600, Kargu-2, Lancet-3, Shahed-136) are fooled into landing as airframes you can pick up (50% health); FPVs, fibre FPVs and EW quads have no GPS and fly straight through; your own GPS drones land too
Counter-drone turret 2×2, range 26; only engages hostile drones, no line of sight needed (only avoids thick rock roofs), head tracks the target; with CE it needs 35mm ammo (see below)

💡Tip

🏠 Roofs stop explosions and drones cannot see through roofs — a roofed machine room is air defence.

⏰ When enemy drones show up

Timing Condition
Before the research Until you research Autonomous munitions, an industrial-or-above raid arms only 1 raider (2 at 1,500+ points) with a single FPV or Switchblade 300 and a small policy — guns can shoot it down, and it tells you what to research. The dedicated drone raid event does not happen yet
Dedicated event One is guaranteed 1.5–3 days after the research finishes; after that at 500+ threat points, player home map, industrial or above factions (tribals never). Chance 1.2, 10-day refire
Any raid Hostile humanlike factions of industrial tech or above arm 10% of their people (at least 1) about 90 ticks after landing; the dedicated drone raid uses 15–50% by doctrine. Tribal, neolithic, medieval, mechanoids and insects never
Drones each 1–3 by doctrine (3-slot back rack); one operator in every three carries an EW quad instead of one attack airframe
Enemy jamming (after the research) Handheld jammers: one per 10 raiders (at least 1, at most 4; ×2 for spacer factions such as the Empire), carried by non-operators; when your radio-linked drones come within 9 cells they switch on for 30 seconds and drop them, then recharge for about 2 hours. Jammer tower: siege raids put one up at their camp (radius 18, no power needed, hits everyone's drones). Neither can touch fibre-optic FPVs
Launch timing About 5 seconds after entering the map, or as soon as a colonist is within 45 tiles; inside 14 tiles they back off to 22 tiles first. Fiber-optic FPV is the exception: it flies on a 40-tile cable, so it is launched only once a colonist is within 36 tiles (cable length × 0.9) and never sent out early to scout
Retreat A drone raid retreats once half its people are killed or downed (the whole group panic-flees like a vanilla raid, and their names change to the fleeing color); operators retreat with their team — whether the raiders are satisfied, gave up, are fleeing heavy losses, or are leaving with loot or a kidnapped colonist (half the team leaving also counts) — and their drones are pulled back exactly like yours when you undraft (recoverable ones drop as airframes, one-way ones crash on the spot)
EW quad It has no warhead and never rams anyone: an enemy one flies near your people and circles 3–6 cells out, keeping them inside its jamming radius
Terminal pursuit Within 6 tiles of its locked target a drone steers straight at where the target is right now, so it catches running enemies too; it always detonates on contact (1.5-tile contact fuse), never a tile short — yours too

🎯 Playing with Combat Extended

With Combat Extended (CE) active, this mod switches to "extreme realism" combat values on CE's scale automatically — no settings. Without CE everything stays exactly as before. Each unit is mapped to a real-world item and uses CE's own numbers for that real round or armour (CE armour: sharp in mm, blunt in MPa).

Thing With CE In plain words
Robot Armour sharp 2 / blunt 4 (a service robot, no armour) 9mm goes through
Robot + armour plating Total sharp 10 / blunt 18 (like an NIJ Level III steel plate); plates wear down under fire and are repaired with steel Stops pistols and ball 5.56 / 7.62, not AP
Drone airframes Sharp 0.5 / blunt 1 (Shahed 1 / 2) Any bullet or fragment brings one down
FPV RPG-7 fragmentation warhead: blast 58, radius 1.5, 80 small fragments
Switchblade 300 40mm-grenade class: direct-hit jet (63 sharp pen) + small blast + 20 fragments
Kargu-2 60mm-mortar class: blast 76, radius 2, large and small fragments
Lancet-3 Shaped charge: direct-hit jet (200 sharp pen) + 81mm-mortar-class blast Anti-armour
Switchblade 600 Javelin warhead: direct-hit jet (750 sharp pen) + blast 585 Goes through anything
Shahed-136 Bigger than a 155mm shell: blast 800, radius 7, 180 fragments Takes out half a base
Counter-drone turret 35mm AA gun: 169 damage per hit + an 87 secondary blast; needs 35mm HE (make "35x228mm HE" at CE's ammo bench or buy it; holds 320, 2 per burst, haulers reload it) A new turret starts empty
Fire-coordination model Now mostly aiming accuracy (+0.15 to +0.50), a little weapon handling (+0.05 to +0.12) AI fire control fixes lead and range
Sensor suite Aiming accuracy +0.20, night vision +0.40 Laser rangefinder + thermal

⚠️Warning

💥 Drones are extremely lethal under CE, and a few things work differently: - Enemy drone raids get ×0.6 points (smaller waves), and Shahed only shows up in raids of 3,500+ points. Even so, a single Lancet or Switchblade 600 kills any colonist — jammers, counter-drone turrets and roofs are not optional. - A drone with a warhead that gets shot down cooks off 25% of the time (blast + fragments). Mind what is underneath it. - Fragments fly further than the blast, so your drones want friendlies further away before they commit (blast radius × 2). - Roofs still stop the blast itself, but CE's wall spall means a blast against a wall can throw fragments into the room and lightly wound people inside (turn off "Fragments from walls" in CE's settings if you don't want that). - Robots with guns reload and pick up ammo under CE's rules, the same as colonists. - Don't add or remove CE mid-save — that is a CE limitation (ammo, inventory). This mod's values are not stored in the save; they are picked from the mod list at startup.

13. Events

Event Options and consequences
🎯 Datacenter raid Only large compute attracts one; they are after your weight cartridges
🔓 Cyber intrusion Cut the network (cluster down a day) / trace back (a coin flip) / keep operating
💧 Coolant leak Spend 4 barrels to patch it now / hold on and re-lay the pipe later
📋 Export control audit Hand over half / refuse and take a reputation hit / pay silver to make it go away; chip shortages are 3× as likely for the next 30 days
🏭 Chip shortage Only after AI compute infrastructure is researched; lasts 5–10 days: traders' new accelerator cards are bought up (used cards remain), accelerator prices ×1.5 (used ×1.25); not again for 30 days after it ends
📉 Training loss spike Roll back (lose 20% of progress) / push through (35% chance of a broken model) / abort
🗃️ Data reclamation claim After every 20 units of raw data cleaned: pay a 600-silver licence fee / refuse (−15 goodwill)
🕵️ SLA audit A client remotely inspects a running contract: meeting your tier pays +10%, dropping a tier costs −10%
🧬 Model stolen / your model deployed An enemy carries off a cartridge → a raid using it 15–30 days later; take the "stolen weights" site within 25 days to cancel it (see below)
🌌 Singularity crises One per AGI stage: power targeted / factions demand a halt / sabotage (see "The AGI project")

🧬 Rogue AI: stolen models

When an enemy leaves the map carrying one of your weight cartridges, a "Model stolen" letter arrives:

  • 15–30 days later that faction uses it against you (each cartridge is deployed once):
Stolen cartridge What the enemy gains
Flight autonomy policy Always a drone raid, at your policy's size, with +50% operators
Shooting / melee policy Raiders get +4 Shooting or Melee
Any other policy or buff model A raid 25% larger
Foundation model All of the above
  • Misaligned cartridges: ×1.5 the effect (+6 levels, +40%, +75% operators), but about 20% of the raiders go berserk on arrival and attack whoever is near.
  • Get it back: a "stolen weights" site appears on the world map at the same time (an item stash guarded by that faction), valid for 25 days. Take it and bring the cartridge home and the raid is cancelled.
  • After 60 days the model is obsolete and nothing more comes of it.

14. Noise and NIMBY

🔊 Device sounds

Every device has its own sound, and every unit plays its own: silent when off, quiet when idle, spinning up under load. Racks, NVL16 cabinets and immersion tanks follow their actual load: inference mode, a power cap or missing cards all sound quieter than full-speed training, and overheating pins the fans at maximum.

Type What you hear
Running sounds Rack and NVL16 fans, the immersion tank's liquid and bubbles, switches, the dry cooler's fan wall, cooling tower water, the CDU pump, air handler, charging station, the jammer's static, the edge relay's data chirps, the cartridge reader (while loaded), the corpus robot (while training), the backup generator, the operations console keyboard, the small modular reactor (transformer and coolant pumps), the battery station (inverters and climate control, following charge and discharge)
Events Generator start and stop, UPS switchover, contract completed, cartridge inserted, checkpoint write, NOC alert (a rack on the LAN overheating, broken down or without power), swarm launch, jammer kill, counter-drone burst, gas suppression discharge, datacenter alarm, card burnout, card failure, reactor scram

💡Tip

Too loud, or want more of it: Options → Mod settings → AI Compute Infrastructure → AI Compute sound volume (0–100%), which also covers drone flight.

  • Noise looks at where colonists' beds are, not where they are standing: radius 12 with linear falloff, three complaint levels at −3 / −7 / −12 mood.
  • Racks and generators have a noise overlay gizmo: it colourises the map (🟢 audible / 🟡 too loud to sleep / 🔴 sleeping in the machine room) with numbers near the cursor.
Noise source Strength
Air-cooled rack 1.0 (NVL16-class 2.0)
Cold-plate liquid rack ×0.6
Immersion compute vat 0 — not a single fan inside
Backup generator (running) 3.0
Dry cooler 2.0 (one more reason to put it outdoors)

📘Note

NIMBY fires once per scale threshold rather than draining goodwill daily: thresholds at 5,000 / 15,000 / 40,000 peak TFLOPS, −8 goodwill each. Halved once model alignment is done, doubled while you hold a misaligned model; ×1.2 per cooling tower and ×1.3 per small modular reactor; then multiplied by the colony's carbon grade (A ×0.5 to E ×1.5).

🤝 Community fund and green reputation

  • Community fund (contract terminal button): donate silver to your neighbours — 30 silver per 1,000 TFLOPS of peak compute (at least 200), halved while a heat recovery vent is running (you already heat the neighbourhood). Lasts 30 days: NIMBY thresholds ×1.5, backlash ×0.5, and non-hostile factions gain +3 goodwill right away; you cannot donate again until it runs out.
  • Green reputation: once NIMBY has noticed you, every 15 days non-hostile factions gain +2 / +1 / 0 / −1 / −3 goodwill by the colony's carbon grade (A–E). New notification category "Carbon and community".

15. Common pitfalls

📘Note

Check them in order — the answer is usually in the first three.

  1. Panel says "connected the supply pipe, but not the return pipe" → you need both cold and hot.
  2. A kilowatt-class card (≥900 W) sits at 25% → it has no coolant loop, so it self-throttles. That is protection, not a bug.
  3. Still hot after plumbing liquid cooling → open "Cooling plan". Usually pumping (CDU 300) is fine but rejection (dry cooler 600) is short, or the dry cooler is indoors and derating itself.
  4. A model tier cannot be selected, or a training rack says "not contributing" → not enough HBM on that network (large needs 1,600 GB; colossal needs 5,000 GB, which means an NVL16). Cards only add up when their racks are on the same network.
  5. Training will not move → not enough data for that domain (the panel shows one line per domain). Training only uses data inside a data corpus on its LAN: check the corpus is cabled to this LAN, refilling is on and you have that domain's data in stock; if not, add bills for it at the annotation bench. Synthetic data alone also stalls: it only covers up to half, the rest must be real.
  6. No cluster bonus → cable must run under the racks, and only switches bridge runs.
  7. The grid browns out on startup → rack inrush is 2.5×. Build a UPS; a backup generator only saves you from sustained deficit.
  8. Device switches seem dead → the vanilla flickable switch cuts power; this mod's on/off switch is a separate control. The rack panel's first line says what it is doing or why it is not; the second reads "has power — state: running / standby / off / stalled / broken".
  9. Cards keep dying → rack servicing is its own column in the Work tab ("datacenter ops", right of If nobody has it ticked while racks go unserviced, the operations console's "Next steps" and alerts remind you. Construction) — tick it for someone. A card's first 5 days run at 3×, and it ages to ×1.5 at 120 days and ×2 at 240 (check "Card age" on the rack panel and use "Eject ≥ 120/240-day cards"); have someone do rack servicing (halves the rate for five days); Tier IV halves it again.
  10. Sleeping next to the machine room hurts mood → the 12-tile radius is measured from beds. Immersion vats are silent.
  11. ⚠️ Never recall or undeploy a one-way airframe over your own base → Lancet-3 and Shahed-136 crash and detonate where they are (3×3 footprint, full warhead damage). Only recoverable types fold into items.
  12. A misaligned model costs nothing until a rack is serving it; then it takes 15% of your compute, and the "watched" mood follows once it is revealed (by evaluation or time in service). 15% of your cluster compute vanished for no visible reason → an unevaluated cartridge is probably misaligned. Evaluate it.
  13. Rack servicing is a pure bonus — skip it and the racks run normally, just at the base failure rate.
  14. Racks stopped serving a cartridge and the reader's eject button is greyed out → that cartridge is licensed (locked in its reader). Unlist it under "Licensing & open weights" at the contract terminal.
  15. Colonists lost their buff after taking an inference contract → the contract's reserved capacity comes first and colonists get the rest. Build another inference rack to keep both.
  16. The tier suddenly dropped to Tier II → a room with racks has no automatic fire suppression (research datacenter fire safety and build a gas suppression system, or place a vanilla firefoam popper).
  17. Certified Tier IV but no Tier IV contracts → measured availability is too low (too many outages in the last 30 days); see the line on the terminal.

17. A suggested first playthrough

# Do this What you learn
1 Microelectronics basics → AI compute infrastructure → buy 3 used cards, refurbish into 2 good ones The basic acquisition route
2 Build a rack, slot the cards, power it, switch to Research How automatic research feels
3 Datacenter engineering → cable + cluster switch → grow to 4 racks (+18%) The scale bonus
4 Both coolant pipes + a CDU + a dry cooler outdoors The three cooling layers
5 Machine learning → annotation bench + checkpoint array + train a small model Datasets are the real bottleneck
6 Cartridge → rack in inference mode → your first colonist buff Why physicalisation matters
7 Compute brokerage → take your first contract What a deadline costs
8 Assembly bay + charging dock → your first robot (crafting or construction policy) Compute becomes labour
9 Next-gen accelerator architecture → NVL16 (make sure cooling and power keep up) The value of density
10 Model alignment → Autonomous munitions ⚠️ Before this research, industrial raids already bring 1–2 stray drones (guns can shoot them down); after it, enemies bring more, plus handheld jammers — build jammers and counter-drone turrets first

18. Other mechanics and rules

This chapter gathers rules that are scattered elsewhere or only visible on in-game panels.

🗂️ Training jobs window

Open it with "Training jobs" on a compute rack, a cartridge reader or the operations console (same window; opened from a cartridge on a reader, it lists only what that cartridge can do).

Area What it shows
Top The LAN's current job, progress and queue (picking another job queues it), cancel and clear queue
Categories on the left Train a new model / From a cartridge (rework an existing cartridge) / Evaluation and alignment (incl. re-alignment) / Policy fine-tuning (robot and drone policies) / Data (jobs that need a data domain) / AGI project
Each row Source cartridge, cost (rack-days; evaluation uses inference-pool seat-days), data needed, estimated days at current compute
Buttons "Start" or "Queue" when possible; greyed out with the reason otherwise (missing data, research, no NOC wall on the LAN…)

📘Note

A LAN without a NOC wall cannot train (the window says so). "Extended training" doubles the compute and data; the cartridge then takes 60 days to drop a tier instead of 30.

🧯 Hardware failures and firmware

Rule Numbers
Base failure rate 1/60 per running card per day; a fully loaded 4-card rack loses a card about every 15 days air-cooled, ×0.6 with cold plates (≈25 days), ×0.3 immersed (≈50 days)
Card age (each card tracks its own runtime) Under 5 days infant mortality ×3, 5–120 days ×1, 120+ days ×1.5 (value ×0.75), 240+ days ×2 (value ×0.5)
Other factors Heat raises it; datacenter maintenance (its own work-tab column, uses Construction) halves failures for 5 days and halves the infant period; Tier IV halves it; duty desks and firmware also count
Replacing cards With a card model chosen on the rack and auto-fill on, haulers swap in spares from storage — so keep making or buying cards
Firmware updates A new version about every 8 days (letter). Press "Apply firmware update" on any rack: the whole cluster goes offline for about 2 hours, then gets +5% until the next version; left uninstalled 4 days after release, failures ×1.25

⚡ Power surges

The moment a rack goes from idle to computing, it draws 2.5× power for about 8 seconds (standard rack 2,600 → 6,500 W; NVL16 23,000 → 57,500 W). If the grid cannot take it, it trips — a breach when you are fulfilling a contract. Absorb surges with batteries, UPS and backup generation, or start racks in batches.

🧠 Model obsolescence

A model drops one tier every 30 days (60 for extended-training cartridges) and stops at small. Retraining at the same scale or running "continue pre-training" (half the compute, a quarter of the data) resets the clock. The cartridge panel says "state of the art · drops a tier in X" or "obsolete".

🏭 Where chips come from

Source Rule
Fabricate One fabrication-bench batch of 4 cards' materials gives 4 good cards
Used accelerator cards Traders sell them (value 240); they cannot go into a rack directly — 3 used + 1 component refurbish into 2 good cards at a machining table (starting at 120 days of runtime)
Chip shortage event Only after AI compute infrastructure research; 5–10 days: traders' new cards sell out, new cards ×1.5 value, used ×1.25; three times as likely for 30 days after an export-control audit

🔔 Notifications and mod settings

Options → Mod settings → AI Compute Infrastructure:

Setting Effect
Mode per notification type Card failure, overheat, surge, network down, failover, facility, training, inference jobs, contracts, firmware, robots, drones, fire alarm, carbon, market — each "default / letter / message / off"
Mod sound volume 0–100%, drone flight sounds included
First-time explanations A letter the first time each of ten event types happens (sent once)
Error report prompt When this mod logs an error, asks whether to open the report page

🌐 Multiplayer

Supports RimWorld Multiplayer (zetrith's): works fine without it; with it, load this mod after Multiplayer. Every button, right-click option and dialog action is synced to all players. In multiplayer, notifications always use their default mode (settings are per computer, and showing a letter on one side only would desync).
